agent_note: HIGH CONFIDENCE PAST. 23 event quotes, 23 past / 0 present (100%). 30 dialogue, 7 gnomic, 1 dropped duplicate. NO SINGLE QUOTE FLIPS THE LABEL - the past evidence is unanimous and includes unfakeable specific-scene narration ('Then she continued to walk away', 'The grass was tall in all three fields'). Retrospective narrating situation is marked explicitly in the text, not inferred: 'as I have said' (q06212), 'I believe now' (q06190), 'Until recently, I didn't think' (q06163), 'I even think, at that moment' (q06185) - a narrator recounting from a later vantage. NOT in the 70-85% present band. THE ONE STRUCTURAL RISK, stated plainly: 30 of 61 quotes are dialogue, and a large share of those arrive with quotation marks stripped by the scrape, so the bucketing rested on internal evidence rather than punctuation. Many are present-tense first-person, and had I read them as narration instead of speech the book would have looked mixed. I did not, on four independent grounds visible in the text: (1) vocatives - 'Klara', 'Ricky', 'Chrissie', 'sir', 'Mrs Arthur'; (2) explicit speech markers - 'All I'm saying is', 'I'm not saying', 'I used to act, you know'; (3) speakers who refer to 'my daughter' (q06172) and 'my mother' (q06184), which the AF narrator cannot say; and (4) q06219 reproduces the tail of q06179 WITH quotation marks and a reply, confirming that passage is speech. Every quote in this sample where narration is unambiguous is past tense; there is not one unambiguous present-tense narration quote in 61. Two dedup failures: q06214 is a pure substring of q06163 (I bucketed it unclear so it is not double-counted), and q06179/q06219 partially overlap.
